item.title: I give kudos to people who sent me to jail; it’s like school – Orji Kalu
item.description: Senator representing Abia North, Orji Kalu, has praised those responsible for his imprisonment, saying the six months he spent behind bars gave him valuable life lessons and made him a more humble person. Kalu said rather than regret his incarceration, he considers it an experience that changed his understanding of life and helped him develop a different outlook. The former Abia State governor made the remarks during an interview on Arise Television on Monday. Explaining why he was grateful for the experience, Kalu said, “It made me more humble. It made me to realise that life is not the same thing I used to think about. So I’m very grateful to God I was there.” He added, “And I gave kudos to people that sent me there because it’s like going to school. And I graduated there, and I’m very happy I went there.” Kalu was convicted by a Federal High Court in Lagos in December 2019 on a 39-count charge and sentenced to 12 years’ imprisonment. However, the Supreme Court overturned the conviction on May 8, 2020, ruling that the trial judge, Mohammed Idris, lacked jurisdiction to deliver the judgment after his elevation to the Court of Appeal. The apex court ordered a fresh trial, and Kalu was released from Kuje Correctional Centre after spending approximately six months in custody. Asked whether he believed the conviction was justified, the senator disagreed but said he did not wish to dwell on the matter. “No, it wasn’t the right thing to do. But I don’t like to discuss this because the judge had his reasons. When the judge did it, I praised him. I support all his decisions,” he said. Kalu also acknowledged that the judiciary had its challenges but maintained that some judges remained committed to dispensing justice. He advised Nigerians dissatisfied with rulings of lower courts to pursue appeals rather than publicly condemn judicial decisions. According to him, taking cases to higher courts gives litigants another opportunity to obtain justice, as more judges are involved in reviewing the decisions. item.title: Atiku congratulates Nigerian athletes on three Dakar Youth Olympic gold medals
item.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has congratulated Nigerian athletes following their historic performance at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, where Team Nigeria won three gold medals in athletics. Atiku, in a post on his X account on Tuesday, particularly celebrated Rosemary Nwankwo, Gift Bright and Praise Ugoh for their victories in the women’s 100 metres, men’s 100 metres and women’s 400 metres events, respectively. He described the athletes’ performance as historic, noting that Nwankwo and Bright won the women’s and men’s 100 metres titles on the same day, marking the first time Nigeria had recorded such a double at the Youth Olympic Games. He also congratulated Ugoh for winning the women’s 400 metres title in her first final over the distance at the competition, becoming the first Nigerian to claim the event’s gold medal at the Games. “These young Nigerians have shown the world what discipline, courage and self-belief can achieve. Their success is a reminder that our nation’s greatest wealth lies in her youth, and that when we invest in their talent, they will raise our flag on every stage,” Atiku said. The former vice-president pledged to continue advocating support for young Nigerians, particularly in providing facilities and opportunities for talented individuals to excel. He also congratulated the athletes’ coaches and families, describing their achievements as a source of pride for the country. item.title: Petrol, Food Prices Rise Further As Iran War Worsens El Niño Impact Globally — UN
item.description: El Niño disrupts global weather patterns, bringing heavy rain to some regions and drought to others, and spiking food and fuel prices, a situation worsened by the ongoing war in Iran, according to the Chief Economist at the United Nations’ Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), Maximo Torero. Speaking with AFP, Torero said both rain and drought can impact harvests and production of crops for animal feed. Floods can be particularly devastating, destroying stored food and damaging the infrastructure and transportation needed to get products to market. All these elements can push up prices, and the impacts “can emerge well before harvests are completed,” he said. “Markets react to expectations of future shortages and uncertainty itself can generate volatility,” he told AFP. This year’s El Niño impacts are exacerbated by price shocks caused by the war in Iran, which have raised the cost of fuel and fertiliser for farmers and impacted household spending globally. “For vulnerable households, even moderate food price increases can have huge consequences,” said Torero. “Poor families spend a large share of their incomes on food and therefore have limited capacity to absorb price shocks and spikes,” he added. The consequences can include reduced food consumption, poorer quality diets and “ultimately, increased food insecurity and malnutrition,” he said. In September, the FAO said it had received just one-fifth of the $202 million it requested to prepare for an El Niño-linked food crisis in 22 high-risk countries. Milton Varela, 29, poses for a picture on a flooded street after heavy rains in Pucallpa, Peruvian Amazon on March 22, 2025. Impacts Around The World This Week An exceptionally strong El Niño is driving weather disruptions around the globe, stoking food security fears and increasing the chances that 2026 will be the second-hottest year on record, experts say. Here is how the climate phenomenon has been playing out around the world in the last week. People walk from a market while balancing their purchased food and household supplies on their heads in Ifotaka, in southern Madagascar, on September 23, 2026. Photo by RAZAFINDRAKOTO MAMY NIRINA / AFP Heat Record The world is on track for 2026 to be the second-hottest year on record, with the El Niño weather pattern turbocharging human-driven global warming, the European Union’s climate monitor said Friday. “October has continued the pattern of remarkable global warmth, with record global and surface ocean temperatures,” said Samantha Burgess, strategic lead for climate at the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, which operates the Copernicus monitor. “An exceptionally strong El Niño is adding further heat to a climate already warmed by human activities,” she said. item.title: 2027: Tinubu will win, he has no competition — Orji Kalu
item.description: Former Abia State Governor and Senator representing Abia North, Orji Uzor Kalu, has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu will win re-election in 2027, declaring that the President has no serious political challenger. Kalu made the prediction on Monday during an appearance on Arise PrimeTime, the flagship evening current affairs programme of Arise News Television, where he defended Tinubu’s economic reforms and declared that Nigeria’s economy had stabilised. The former Senate Chief Whip, who chairs the Senate Committee on the South East Development Commission, also defended the administration against criticism over the economic hardship associated with its policies. He argued that Tinubu had stabilised the economy at the macroeconomic level, saying the major challenge now was to translate that progress into improved living conditions for households and businesses. “President Tinubu has been able to stabilise this economy on the macro level. What we are battling now, having stabilised the economy on the macro level, is the micro level,” he said. Kalu said the administration’s next priority should be to boost agricultural production, improve security and create an enabling environment for manufacturers to access raw materials and increase production capacity. Acknowledging the economic difficulties facing Nigerians, he maintained that the country was beginning to experience greater economic predictability, arguing that reforms often come with temporary hardships. He also credited Tinubu with improving Nigeria’s international economic relations, saying the country was increasingly attracting the attention of foreign investors. On the 2027 presidential election, the senator dismissed the opposition’s chances, insisting that Tinubu would secure another four-year term. “President Tinubu will win. President Tinubu has no competition. The APC’s electoral strength goes beyond the personality of the President. The ruling party enjoys a broad political structure and substantial grassroots support across the country. “What we are seeing on social media is not what is on the ground. Our party is very huge, and the supporters of that party are large. We have huge numbers of people supporting this party,” he said. Kalu added that APC lawmakers and other political stakeholders were already mobilising to consolidate the party’s electoral strength in their respective constituencies ahead of the election. He also appealed for political stability, urging Nigerians to prioritise national unity and allow elected presidents to complete their constitutionally permitted terms. “The unity of this country is very important. Let’s not question the unity. We allowed President Buhari to do his eight years and go, and we must allow Tinubu to do his eight years and go,” he said. item.title: I sold heavy weapons internationally – Orji Kalu
item.description: …Says he sold arms to anyone who could buy The Senator representing Abia North, Orji Kalu, has disclosed that he previously engaged in the international trade of heavy weapons, selling arms to buyers in different countries before quitting the business at the insistence of his parents. Kalu made the revelation during an interview on Arise Television on Monday, while discussing his business background and relationships with former and current South African leaders. Asked whether he was an arms dealer, the former Abia State governor answered in the affirmative, saying he stopped after his parents intervened. “Yes, so I stopped because my parents, my mother, my father came and said I must stop, and I stopped,” he said. Asked whether he sold weapons to people who intended to use them to kill others, Kalu dismissed the suggestion, saying his motivation was to make money. “No, no, no, no, no, no. I was selling guns to make money, whether they blow up it’s not my business,” he said. The interviewer subsequently asked whether he supplied weapons to the African National Congress (ANC) during its struggle against apartheid in South Africa. Kalu said he did not restrict his business to the ANC, explaining that he sold weapons to any buyer who could afford them. “No, I was selling to anybody who wants to buy. If you have the money, you want to buy in D.R.C, I sell to you, you want to buy in Namibia, you want to buy…” he said. Asked about the source of the weapons, the senator declined to provide details, saying, “It’s only my business.” The interviewer also questioned how his former arms trade related to Nigeria’s current security challenges and the proliferation of small arms. In response, Kalu clarified that the weapons he traded were not small arms but heavy weapons sold between countries. “No, these are heavy arms that were sold country to country,” he said. Asked specifically whether he sold weapons to Libya under its late leader, Muammar Gaddafi, Kalu said he sold to anyone with the financial capacity to purchase them. “To anybody that had money to buy,” he responded. When the interviewer suggested that his answer meant he had supplied weapons to Gaddafi, Kalu replied, “May his soul rest in peace. He was a good man. If you have money to buy, when I was selling, I would sell to you.” The senator also spoke about his relationships with successive South African presidents, tracing the connections to his friendship with the country’s late former president, Nelson Mandela. He said Mandela introduced him to several South African leaders, including former President Thabo Mbeki and incumbent President Cyril Ramaphosa. According to Kalu, Mandela once told him that Mbeki’s father had contributed more to the anti-apartheid struggle than Ramaphosa’s father. He said the consideration influenced the ANC’s decision to select Mbeki ahead of Ramaphosa as Mandela’s running mate. item.title: 2027: Most Christians we’ve engaged are okay with Muslim-Muslim ticket – Yilwatda
item.description: The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Nentawe Yilwatda, says most Christians consulted by the party have expressed satisfaction with the Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket of President Bola Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima ahead of the 2027 general elections. Yilwatda said Christians’ initial concerns that the arrangement could marginalise them had not materialised, insisting that their voices remained represented in the administration. The APC chairman stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday. “Most Christians that we’ve engaged and we’ve spoken to them, they are very okay with the Muslim-Muslim ticket,” he said. “The thought and the fear of most Christians was that the Muslim-Muslim ticket may suppress their voices, but their voices are heard loud and clear now.” He also dismissed concerns that Tinubu’s religion had exposed Christians to discrimination or persecution during his three years in office. On questions surrounding the President’s health and fitness to contest the 2027 election, Yilwatda maintained that Tinubu was physically capable of seeking re-election. He also defended the President’s decision not to attend every campaign rally, arguing that his constitutional responsibilities would not allow him to participate in all party engagements. According to him, some government officials have been advised to attend selected rallies to ensure that governance is not affected by campaign activities. On the leadership crisis rocking the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Yilwatda denied allegations that the APC was behind the party’s internal dispute following the Federal High Court judgment invalidating the David Mark-led leadership. He questioned the opposition party’s decision to blame the ruling party over a dispute arising from a legal action instituted by one of its members. The APC chairman further expressed confidence that Tinubu would defeat former Vice President Atiku Abubakar in a free and fair election. He attributed Atiku’s performance in the 2023 presidential election largely to the political structure of the Peoples Democratic Party rather than his personal popularity. “He did not win because of Atiku; he won because of the structure of the PDP. It was the PDP that brought Atiku, not Atiku winning on his own,” Yilwatda said. He also defended FCT Minister Nyesom Wike’s proposed ₦10m reward for councils that deliver their wards for Tinubu in 2027, arguing that the incentive did not constitute vote buying. item.title: Edo LGA orders daily bush surveillance ahead of Yuletide
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Chairman of Etsako East Local Government Area of Edo State, Rt. Hon. Sunny Ekpetika Ekpeson, has directed vigilante groups to intensify daily surveillance and comb bushes and forests across the area ahead of the Christmas and New Year celebrations. Ekpeson, who is also the Edo State Chairman of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria (ALGON), gave the directive during an emergency security meeting with vigilante leaders and coordinators to address security concerns ahead of the festive season. A statement issued on Monday, November 9, 2026, by Agbukor Lucky Apeakhuye, the chairman’s media aide on Politics and Strategic Development, said the meeting focused on strengthening security operations across Etsako East. According to the statement, Ekpeson directed vigilante operatives to conduct daily surveillance and thoroughly comb bushes, forests and identified security flashpoints to prevent criminal elements from using remote locations as hideouts. The chairman warned that kidnapping, killings, cult-related activities, violence and other criminal acts would not be tolerated anywhere in the local government area. He also charged security coordinators to strengthen intelligence gathering, improve collaboration among their teams and ensure adequate security coverage across communities throughout the festive period. Those at the meeting included the Vice Chairman, Comrade Charles Aloaye Dagana; Secretary to the Local Government, Dr. Samuel Oshiole Enaboakpe; and Chief Adolphus Oshole Osimi, General Officer Commanding of the Agenebode Zonal Vigilante Command, who oversees security operations across villages in the Weppa-Wanno axis. Other vigilante coordinators also attended the meeting. The statement said Ekpeson reiterated that the protection of lives and property remained a priority of his administration, urging security operatives to remain vigilant, proactive and responsive to distress calls. He further charged vigilante leaders to ensure that the directives translated into concrete action, saying he would not want reports of kidnapping, killings, cult-related violence or other criminal activities across the local government. The meeting, according to the statement, formed part of the council’s measures to strengthen security and ensure peaceful Christmas and New Year celebrations in Etsako East. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 10, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian naira traded with modest movements across both official and parallel foreign exchange markets on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, as market participants weighed ongoing liquidity management by the Central Bank of Nigeria against persistent demand for foreign currency. At the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the United States dollar exchanged at an average rate of ₦1,346.51. The official window recorded early trading activity holding within a narrow band between ₦1,343.35 and ₦1,347.32 per dollar, maintaining the relative stability seen over recent trading sessions. Meanwhile, activities in the parallel market showed the dollar trading between ₦1,410 and ₦1,430 for buying and selling transactions depending on location and local currency dealer. The figures reflect an unofficial market premium of approximately ₦64 to ₦83 per dollar over the NFEM spot rate. Financial analysts note that the mild divergence between official rate outcomes and informal channels continues to reflect spot demand from small-scale importers and individual retail buyers seeking prompt foreign currency access outside primary banking channels. Overall market conditions remain anchored by broader foreign reserve levels and regular clearing of foreign trade obligations. item.title: Asaba rally death: Okada, Keke operators offer police evidence
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi ASABA — Commercial motorcycle and tricycle operators in Delta State have offered to provide video footage and other relevant evidence to assist the police in identifying and prosecuting those responsible for the alleged killing of Chinaza Sunday during Saturday’s political violence in Asaba. The operators, under the Commercial Motorcycles and Tricycles Operators Association (COMTOA), made the offer on Monday during a protest at the Delta State Police Command headquarters, where they demanded justice for the deceased, whom they identified as a member of their association. Addressing the police on behalf of the association, a member of its Board of Trustees, Prince Okeoghene Miller Kingsley, said Chinaza was carrying out his legitimate business when he was allegedly killed. “The young man that was murdered was at his duty post carrying out his legitimate duty, where he met his untimely death. “We want to believe that we have confidence in the Nigerian Police that they will do justice to this issue and those persons should be brought to book,” he said. Kingsley said the association was prepared to assist investigators with video recordings, relevant information and details of individuals allegedly connected with the incident. He also dismissed suggestions that the deceased or members of the association were involved in criminal activities or political thuggery. “Chinaza has not been an armed robber. He has not been a thug or a political thug. Everybody you are seeing here is going about our lawful duties. Nobody here is a thug,” he declared. Defending the political rights of commercial transport operators, Kingsley said members were free to associate with political parties and movements of their choice. “Everybody here has the right to belong to anybody he likes to belong to because there is freedom of association, which includes lawful assembly,” he added. Responding, the Deputy Commissioner of Police, Administration, Philip Adejo, acknowledged receipt of the protesters’ petition and assured them that the command would investigate the killing. “We have received your petition. Sometimes self-help can become a serious problem. We sympathise with you; go home and rest because you will see results. It is not going to be like other situations,” Adejo said. He urged the association’s leadership to provide credible information that could assist the investigation. “Your leaders can meet us, and if you have any strong information concerning this, you can come to us so that we can iron it out together,” he added. The protest followed violence on Saturday, November 7, along Nnebisi Road, Asaba, during a procession organised by the Obidient/OK Movement in support of Peter Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC). item.title: FG unveils N70bn plan to tackle Noma
item.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Federal Government has unveiled a N70bn National Oral Health Strategic Plan for 2026–2030 to improve access to dental care, address the burden of oral diseases and eliminate Noma as a public health problem. The five-year plan is designed to expand preventive and curative oral health services, improve early detection and treatment of Noma, strengthen the dental workforce and integrate oral healthcare into primary healthcare services across the 774 local government areas. The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako, announced the initiative on Monday in Abuja during the commemoration of National Noma Day and National Oral Health Day. According to a statement by the ministry’s Assistant Director, Information and Public Relations, Ado Bako, Salako said the initiative aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, which prioritises the health and wellbeing of Nigerians. He described oral health as a critical component of Universal Health Coverage, saying it should no longer be neglected in the country’s healthcare delivery system. Expressing concern over Nigeria’s burden of Noma, particularly in the North-West and North-East, the minister described the disease as preventable but devastating, with the potential to cause severe facial disfigurement, disability and death, especially among malnourished children. He said the World Health Organisation’s recognition of Noma as a Neglected Tropical Disease in 2023 marked a significant milestone in global efforts to combat the condition. Salako disclosed that the Federal Ministry of Health had integrated Noma surveillance into the Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response system, while intensifying efforts to improve early detection and referral through primary healthcare facilities. He added that frontline health workers, traditional healers and traditional birth attendants had been trained in 19 states to identify early signs of Noma and other oral diseases and facilitate prompt referrals for treatment. Highlighting gaps in oral healthcare delivery, the minister said more than 80 per cent of Nigerians had never visited a dentist, while two out of every three children were living with untreated dental caries. He further disclosed that Nigeria had approximately one dentist for every 38,000 people, compared with the World Health Organisation’s recommended ratio of one dentist to 7,500 people. To address the challenges, Salako said the government was strengthening the integration of oral healthcare into primary healthcare through the Sector-Wide Approach and the Basic Health Care Provision Fund to improve access to affordable and quality services. He also announced that the Federal Executive Council had approved the National Centre for Oral Health Establishment Bill 2026 and forwarded it to the National Assembly for consideration. item.title: Three Nigerians arrested in India over immigration status
item.description: Three Nigerians have been arrested in Delhi, India, for allegedly residing in the country without valid immigration documents. The Times of India reported on Sunday that the Delhi Police arrested the men during a verification exercise in Dwarka, southwest Delhi, on October 31. The report, which cited police officials, identified the suspects as Bartholomew Iloegbunem, Konan Okocha, also known as Konan Brice Kousaai, and Ndubuisi Nwabufor. According to the report, the three men were unable to produce documents authorising their stay in India when questioned by the police. They were subsequently presented before the Foreigners Regional Registration Office and transferred to the Sewa Sadan detention centre in Lampur. The arrests followed a police verification drive targeting foreign nationals in the area, the newspaper reported. item.title: China Diaries: An Emperor, 8,000 Soldiers and a Lesson for Nigeria!
item.description: I came looking for ancient soldiers and left thinking about Nigeria’s tourism potential! One of the things I was particularly looking forward to during my visit to China was seeing the famous Terracotta Warriors in Xi’an. I had read about them, seen pictures and, of course, watched films inspired by the mysteries of ancient China. But nothing quite prepares you for the experience of standing in front of thousands of life-sized soldiers who have been buried underground for more than 2,000 years. And what an experience it was! For anyone who has watched Hollywood’s The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor, you may remember the mysterious army of clay soldiers that comes alive. Well, I finally got to see the real thing. Thankfully, none of them came alive while I was there! But standing in those enormous exhibition halls, surrounded by thousands of soldiers, horses and chariots arranged in military formation, I couldn’t help wondering what must have gone through the minds of the people who created this extraordinary army. The story takes us back to around 221 BC, when Qin Shi Huang became the first emperor to unify China. Like many powerful rulers of his time, he was obsessed with immortality and the idea of continuing his reign beyond death. His solution was to build an entire underground army to protect him in the afterlife. Think about that! While some people prepare for retirement, this emperor was preparing for eternity, complete with his own military formation! The scale of the project is difficult to comprehend. Thousands of life-sized clay soldiers, horses and chariots were painstakingly created. And what makes the discovery even more fascinating is that the soldiers are not identical. They have different facial features, hairstyles, uniforms and expressions. They look like real individuals, each with a distinct identity and military rank. Then comes another remarkable twist. For over two thousand years, this enormous army remained hidden beneath the earth until 1974, when some local farmers digging a well stumbled upon fragments of what would become one of the greatest archaeological discoveries in modern history. Imagine going out to dig a well and discovering an entire army! I wonder what the conversation was like that evening when they returned home. Today, the site is recognised globally as one of the greatest archaeological treasures in the world and is popularly described as the Eighth Wonder of the World. UNESCO designated the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor a World Heritage Site in 1987. But beyond the fascinating history, what struck me most was what China has done with this discovery. This is where the story becomes particularly interesting for Nigeria. China has not simply uncovered an ancient treasure and left it to gather dust. It has invested in archaeological research, conservation, restoration, museum infrastructure, visitor facilities and tourism development. The preservation work itself is remarkable. item.title: Oluwo seeks Yoruba language as medium for teaching science
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Oluwo of Iwo, Oba Abdulrosheed Akanbi, has called for the development and promotion of Yoruba language as a medium of instruction for academic subjects, including Physics and other specialised courses. The monarch made the call on Monday during the 2026 Odun Olodumare celebration and his 11th coronation anniversary at his palace in Iwo, Osun State. Oba Akanbi said Yoruba had the capacity to serve as a language of instruction across different academic disciplines if deliberate efforts were made to develop and expand its use. “Normally, I prefer to speak my Yoruba language. I want to upgrade the Yoruba language so that we can use it to teach Physics and all kinds of subjects and courses in the educational system,” he said. The traditional ruler also advocated the preservation and modernisation of Yoruba culture, particularly the reform of traditions he said promoted violence. While praising the richness of Yoruba heritage, he stressed the need to preserve its positive aspects while addressing practices that could encourage violence. “When it comes to culture, I want a culture that is free of violence. I accept all Yoruba cultures and traditions, but those that need modifications, particularly traditions that promote violence, must be addressed. “It is not that I totally reject them, but I understand that change takes time,” he said. The monarch also announced a N5 million empowerment scheme for at least 100 residents of Iwo, with each beneficiary expected to receive N50,000. He said the beneficiaries would be drawn from different segments of the community, including members of the royal institution, princes, chiefs, the Muslim community, traditional initiates and ordinary residents. According to him, beneficiaries will be selected randomly rather than through a predetermined process. The 2026 Odun Olodumare celebration also attracted members of different religious groups to the palace, where they offered prayers and praises to God for the monarch, his subjects, Iwo town and the country. item.title: US-mediated talks with Russia and Ukraine to start in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States will hold talks in Abu Dhabi Tuesday on ending Europe’s worst conflict since World War II in the first such meeting in more than nine months, as another winter of war approaches. Europe – alarmed by US President Donald Trump floating a deal with Moscow on European security ahead of the talks – will also send representatives to Abu Dhabi. Trump has pushed for an end to the Russia-Ukraine war since returning to power, but previous talks produced no breakthroughs and the process became sidelined by the US-Israeli war against Iran. Europe and Ukraine fear the United States will force a deal on Kyiv that would amount to a de-facto capitulation, with Trump appearing to pivot towards Moscow this year. Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine has killed hundreds of thousands, displaced millions and has dragged on for 56 months, with the Kremlin showing no sign of backing down. Trump hinted Ukraine will have to give up land ahead of the talks, saying: “They’re going to end up with a little bit different shape, Ukraine.” Russia occupies large swathes of Ukraine but, while its troops have grinded westwards, they have not been able to seize the whole of the Donetsk region. Moscow demands Kyiv surrender the parts of the region it still controls, vowing it will otherwise press on with its offensive. Ukraine – which for more than 4.5 years has resisted a far larger invading army at a huge human cost – has ruled out such a withdrawal. Russia pummelled Ukraine in the run-up to the talks and carried out one of its deadliest strikes yet – with Kyiv saying 55 people were killed in a frontline village as they queued for humanitarian aid. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the intensified strikes were part of Moscow’s strategy of “putting pressure on Ukraine’s position” at the negotiations. Russia’s Vladimir Putin, who launched the war in February 2022, has repeatedly refused broader ceasefire offers and face-to-face talks with Zelensky. Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff will gather the enemy sides in Abu Dhabi for the first time since February, when negotiations took place in Geneva. Russia and Ukraine have held several rounds of failed talks during almost five years of war and hopes for peace are low. “We don’t have any particular expectations,” a senior Ukrainian official in Kyiv told AFP. ‘We don’t want Yalta 2.0’ Trump last week floated a “very big agreement” on the war that will “involve all of Europe”, stoking fears Washington would collaborate with Moscow on creating a new European security architecture. Shortly before launching its 2022 invasion, Moscow had issued an ultimatum to the West for NATO to rollback troops from Eastern Europe. The diplomat who issued the demand, Sergei Ryabkov, will for the first time be part of Moscow’s delegation, which is headed by Putin’s nationalistic aide Vladimir Medinsky. item.title: Rivers community that forbids female dogs explains tradition to NYSC members
item.description: By Davies Iheamnachor — APARA The people of Ekinobo in Apara Kingdom, Ikwerre ethnic nationality of Rivers State, have raised the alarm over the growing disregard for their customs, including a longstanding prohibition against keeping female dogs in the community. •His Royal Majesty Eze Ohna Apara Kingdom, Gift Eziwhuo Johnson (middle), flanked by corps members. The community, located in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area, said urbanization, the influx of strangers and increasing Western influence had contributed to the erosion of its cultural heritage and traditional practices. This came as the Paramount Ruler of Apara Kingdom, His Royal Majesty, Eze Gift Eziwhuo Johnson, Eze Ohna Apara IV, and the Chiefs-in-Council hosted members of the Culture and Tourism Community Development Service (CDS) of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) to a cultural orientation programme on the customs, traditions and laws of the Apara people. The corps members embarked on the visit as part of an initiative to familiarise themselves with the cultural values of their host communities, understand local traditions and avoid practices capable of offending indigenous sensibilities. The visit also provided an opportunity for the traditional institution to seek stronger collaboration with the NYSC in promoting mutual understanding, preserving cultural heritage and fostering peaceful relationships. NYSC members visit Speaking during the visit, the leader of the Culture and Tourism CDS group, Dominic Umoh, said the initiative was designed to expose corps members to the cultural values of their host communities and preserve such knowledge for future generations. He explained that understanding local customs was important because corps members could eventually establish personal and family relationships with people from their places of service. “We might get married to somebody from here, so there is a need for us to understand their culture. We are here to know the dos and don’ts of the Ikwerre people,” he said. Lectures on Iwhuruoha, popularly known as Ikwerre, culture and traditions were delivered by Eze (Dr) Chibuike Wali, Darlington Wigwe, Prof. Nmecha Akani and Chief (Dr) Chinedu Amadi. Commending the corps members, Eze Johnson, who spoke through the Palace Spokesman, Chief Chinedu Amadi, described the engagement as worthwhile and successful, noting that chiefs from different parts of Apara Kingdom attended to demonstrate their support. He said the corps members were educated on several traditional practices, including the prohibition against female dogs and traditional rites associated with deaths occurring on certain days, particularly a day locally known as Iriagbo. “We were able to tell them certain things or certain cultures that are permissible in this part of the world. item.title: I won’t surrender my senatorial ticket — Uzodimma
item.description: Governor Hope Uzodimma of Imo State has insisted that he remains in the 2027 Senatorial race, describing suggestions that he would surrender his ambition to another candidate as “a lie”. Read Also: Court sacks Uzodinma as APC senatorial candidate for Imo West A Federal High Court sitting in Abuja, on October 29, 2026, ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to remove Uzodimma’s name as Senatorial candidate for Imo West and replace it with the name of former Governor Rochas Okorocha. Justice Obiora Egwuatu based the judgment on the grounds that Uzodimma did not win the All Progressives Congress, APC, primary election held on May 18. The outcome of the ruling has since been rejected by the APC in the state, with the party insisting that Uzodimma remains its candidate for Imo West Senatorial District. Speaking on Sunday after attending Mass at the Government House Chapel in Owerri, the Imo state capital, Uzodimma dismissed insinuations that he would cede his ticket to anyone as deceptive. “If they tell you that I will hold this ticket and somebody will collect it and give it to another, tell the person it is a lie,” he said. He called on residents of the state to canvass support for the APC to ensure its victory across all levels, mentioning names of candidates voters should rally round in the forthcoming elections. “Go and campaign for the party, our great party, the All Progressives Congress, APC. There is no other political party we are going with. “For the House of Assembly, it is APC. For the House of Representatives, it is APC,” the governor said. He added, “For the Senate, your senator in Okigwe zone is Patrick Ndubueze, in Orlu zone it is my humble self (Hope Uzodimma), and in Owerri zone it is (Alex) Mbata,” he said. Okorocha Meanwhile, Okorocha had earlier described the ruling nullifying Uzodimma’s candidacy as a victory for the nation’s judiciary and democracy. Okorocha, in a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Media, Sam Onwuemodo, commended President Bola Tinubu for, according to him, providing the enabling environment for the Judiciary and other Institutions to function for the nation’s rapid development and growth. “This judgment, to say the least, is a resounding victory for the nation’s judiciary. It is a victory for the nation’s fast-growing democracy. It is an outstanding victory for the nation’s Constitution, as amended. He added, “It is a remarkable victory for all lovers of what is right and haters of what is wrong. It is a notable victory for posterity and history. “Finally, it is a victory for Imo people in general, and Imo West Senatorial District people in particular.” Vanguard News The post I won’t surrender my senatorial ticket — Uzodimma appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Man hammers father to death in Edo over prophecy
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu, BENIN CITY A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress, APC, in Fugar, Etaako Central Local Government Area, Julius Bello has been killed by his son identified as Irobudo. The Edo State Police Command Police Public Relations Officer, Eno Ikoedem, confirmed the killing. Ikoedem said they had commenced investigation. Irobudo was said to have carried out the action because he was told by a prophet that his father was responsible for his poor state. The suspect was still at large as at press time. The deceased, popularly known as De Lord Ogata, was Ward Three Chairman of the APC in Fugar. He was reportedly killed by his son who used a sledgehammer to hit him on the head. Witnesses said the suspect returned home from Lagos at the weekend and attacked his father on Sunday. item.title: Explainer: Election results collation chain that decides Nigeria’s president
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – Nigeria’s president is not declared on the strength of a single national count. A chain of collation officers, each signing for the votes below them, builds the result from the polling unit up to the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC. Read Also: * Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal * Why getting most votes is not enough to become Nigeria’s president The chain starts when voting ends. Voters are accredited with the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, and the presiding officer counts the ballots in public and enters each party’s score on Form EC8A, the polling unit result sheet. The presiding officer signs the form, and polling agents who are present countersign it. A poster version, Form EC60E, is pasted at the polling unit so voters can see what was recorded. Collation then moves upward. INEC’s then chairman, Mahmood Yakubu, described the 2023 process as running through “four levels”: ward, local government area, LGA, state and national. At each level, an officer adds up the forms from the level below and records the total on a new form. The election results forms The ward collation officer adds up the Form EC8A sheets in the ward and records the total on Form EC8B. The LGA collation officer then adds up the ward sheets on Form EC8C. At state level, the State Collation Officer for the Presidential Election (SCOPE) adds up the LGA results on Form EC8D. Katsina in 2023 shows what that form contains: 3,516,719 registered voters; 1,097,663 accredited; 1,058,673 valid votes, and 32,514 rejected. Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, led with 489,045 votes against 482,283 for Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC. The national stage takes place in Abuja, with the INEC Chairman acting as returning officer for the presidential election. That office is now held by Joash Amupitan, who succeeded Yakubu in October 2025. In 2023, Yakubu set out the procedure at the national collation centre, where each state’s SCOPE presents the original Form EC8D. “When all the SCOPES have presented their results,” the returning officer displays the sealed copies of Form EC8DA, the state-by-state summary, and Form EC8E, the declaration sheet. Polling agents are invited to comment before the winner is declared, and each agent receives duplicate copies afterwards. Declaring winner Declaring the winner involves more than adding up votes. The returning officer must also confirm that the candidate with the highest total reached one-quarter of the votes in enough states, as Section 134 of the Constitution requires. The 2023 totals show the arithmetic. Yakubu put registered voters at 93,469,008; accredited voters at 25,286,616; valid votes at 24,025,940, and rejected votes at 939,278. Tinubu polled 8,794,726; Atiku 6,984,520; Peter Obi of the Labour Party, LP, 6,101,533, and Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party, NNPP, 1,496,687. On the spread test, Tinubu’s lawyer

item.title: Power outages remain despite rise in generation, ministerial promise
item.description: By Udeme Akpan, Ediri Ejoh, Obas Esiedesa & Cynthia Alo Nigeria’s electricity generation rose to 4,020.41 megawatts (MW) on Monday from 3,500MW, but the increase has yet to translate into adequate supply for consumers across the country. This comes as the promise last Thursday by the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, to restore normalcy in power supply within 72 hours expired two days ago. Data obtained from the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) showed that 20 power plants were connected to the national grid as of 1.0pm yesterday, producing a combined 4,020.41MW. The output was below Sunday’s peak generation of 4,253.6MW but above the off-peak figure of 3,862.17MW. Last Thursday, generation had dropped to 3,659MW from 3,996MW recorded the previous day, worsening supply conditions across several parts of the country. Promising restoration within 72 hours, the Ministry of Power had ruled out a major or systemic national grid failure, explaining that preliminary assessments linked the disruptions to maintenance and operational challenges across parts of the power value chain, alongside declining generation. An analysis of Monday’s generation profile showed that Afam VI contributed the highest output of 519MW, followed by Shiroro Hydro Power Plant with 445MW and Azura-Edo Independent Power Plant with 438MW. Egbin Power Plant, with an installed capacity of 1,320MW, contributed 108MW. Meanwhile, load allocation to the 11 electricity distribution companies (DisCos) stood at a combined 3,195MW as of 5:07pm yesterday; Abuja DisCo received 581MW; Ikeja 467MW; Eko 458MW and Ibadan 359MW. Others were Port Harcourt, 294MW; Benin, 243MW; Enugu, 233MW; Kano, 173MW; Kaduna, 167MW; Jos, 146MW; and Yola, 74MW. In his update on the power situation, Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, said electricity had been restored to many communities affected by recent disruptions, particularly in Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Kwara and the Federal Capital Territory. He disclosed that the vandalised Benin-Egbin 330kV transmission line had been repaired and returned to service, helping to raise electricity supply to the Lagos Complex to more than 1,000MW. However, he acknowledged that some locations were still experiencing outages. “Our priority continues to be the provision of reliable electricity to Nigerians,” he said. Speaking on a TVC programme monitored by Vanguard, Tegbe said: “Let me start by telling Nigerians, especially those in the three or four states that were recently affected by the outage, that I feel their pain, and President Bola Tinubu feels your pain. However, we are doing the best we can, and I believe it will get better.” He disclosed that the Federal Government had paid N1.23 trillion out of the N3.3 trillion owed to generation companies (GenCos), leaving about N2 trillion outstanding, which it hoped to settle next year. item.title: 2027: Tinubu’s projects’ll transform South-East economy – Shettima
item.description: *Yari demands 1.2m votes from Ebonyi; Umahi promises 1.3m *‘If Tinubu isn’t re-elected, ongoing projects’ll stop’ — Uzodimma *APC has built Nigeria for benefit of few — Makinde *PRP accuses APC of suffocating opposition, exploiting religious fault lines By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Omeiza Ajayi, Ndahi Marama & Luminous Jannamike Vice President Kashim Shettima has said President Bola Tinubu’s massive investments in security, infrastructure, agriculture and human capital development are transforming the South-East economy, promising to address the region’s longstanding development challenges. Shettima, who spoke yesterday at the All Progressives Congress, APC, presidential campaign rally in Abakaliki, Ebonyi State, said the Federal Government’s interventions were aimed at improving connectivity, strengthening food security, expanding economic opportunities and restoring security. He said the administration had demonstrated its commitment to Ebonyi through major infrastructure projects, federal appointments and welfare programmes. “This campaign has been a season of triumph. We have triumphed over the falsehoods of our opponents. We have never turned our backs on you. We have answered your support with projects, and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has honoured Ebonyi through distinguished appointments and projects across the state,” he said. According to him, Ebonyi has benefited from the dividends of democracy and deserves to renew the President’s mandate. “You have stood by us. You have assured us that a mandate is a debt of honour, repayable only through service. Yet democracy demands the humility of asking again. We have returned to seek the renewal of your mandate, to serve you, defend you and stand by you,” he added. Listing the Federal Government’s infrastructure projects, Shettima identified the Calabar–Ebonyi–Benue–Kogi–Nasarawa–Abuja Superhighway, part of the administration’s Trans-Saharan highway vision, as a major initiative to strengthen trade between the South-East, North-Central and other regions. Others are the Ndibe Bridge, which will link Ebonyi with Cross River State; the Enugu–Abakaliki–Ogoja Expressway; and the Okposi–Ohaozara–Ukawu–Cross River road. He said the projects would ease the transportation of agricultural produce and manufactured goods, improve market access and reduce business costs. On agriculture, the Vice President described Ebonyi as a major contributor to national food security through rice and cassava production. He listed fertiliser distribution, interest-free FarmerMoni assistance and rural road investments among measures to support farmers. He also disclosed that thousands of Ebonyi residents had benefited from grants under the Presidential Conditional Grant Scheme, while federal employment and digital skills programmes were creating opportunities for youths. item.title: Flamingos: Presidency, Obi bicker over access to players at Abuja airport
item.description: *NFF officials stopped me from greeting Flamingos, Obi *Don’t politicise sports, Presidency tells NDC *Keyamo accuses him of hypocrisy By Henry Umoru ABUJA—THE Media Office of the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, alleged yesterday he was stopped by officials of the Nigeria Football Federation, NFF, from greeting the victorious women’s Under-17 World Champions at Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, on arrival of the team from Morocco, venue of the tournament. Read Also: U-17 WWC: How we overcame opening defeat to win title – Oluebube The Presidency in a swift reaction, faulted the NDC presidential candidate’s claim, even as the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, accused him of hypocrisy. But in a statement signed by spokesperson of Peter Obi Media Office, POMO, Idris Zekeri , the office said the former Anambra State governor was at the airport on his way to Enugu and saw the team that had just arrived. It explained that as Obi tried to greet the players, officials of the NFF pleaded with him to save their jobs. The Media Office said in his usual character, Obi respected their position but described the situation on his X handle as a new dimension of toxic politics in Nigeria. Quoting the NDC presidential hopeful, the statement read: ‘’This is the new dimension of toxic politics that Nigeria has developed since 2025. “I arrived at the airport at 7 a.m. this morning (yesterday) to board my flight to Enugu. There, I saw the Nigeria Under-17 girls’ team, which had just arrived and was preparing to board its vehicle into town. “With genuine joy and enthusiasm, I asked my protocol officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether I could greet and welcome the team. I was informed that officials of the Nigerian Football Federation, NFF, had refused and had requested that I should not approach them because, if I did, they would all lose their jobs. “Regrettably, this is not the first time I have been subjected to such treatment. On March 25, 2025, I was in Uyo for the World Cup qualifier. The governor warmly received me and welcomed me at the VIP stand. ‘’Following the match, other government officials went to greet the players, but I was again prevented from doing so. I was told by the officials that they would lose their jobs if I proceeded. “It is deeply troubling to witness the extent of toxic politics into which our nation has descended since 2025. Each year appears to bring further deterioration. This reflects how deeply Nigeria has been affected. “The new Nigeria we aspire to build must have no room for hostility, intimidation or discrimination, regardless of political affiliation. It must be a Nigeria in which unity, mutual respect and our shared humanity take precedence over political differences. item.title: Tinubu, Atiku, Obi Will Collapse Under Their Own Weight — SDP’s Adewole
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Adewole Adebayo, has said he is confident of victory in a free, fair, and credible 2027 election. Adebayo said that other candidates like President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Atiku Abubakar of the Africa Democratic Party (ADC) and Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Party (NDC) will fall under their own weight. Speaking during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, he said that his manifesto, Farewell to Poverty and Insecurity, is a pathway to progress and good governance that can be deployed to improve the lives of Nigerians “They will collapse under their own weight; that is not the issue. What I want to defeat is poverty and insecurity. “But to defeat that, you need to defeat ignorance in people going to just vote based on sentiment or looking for something,” Adebayo said. “You also have to defeat lethargy where people get tired, ‘Oh, my vote doesn’t count. You also have to defeat apathy. “So, once we do that, we will defeat anybody. When we say defeat, it’s not a wrestling match; it’s about convincing the majority of your fellow citizens to believe in this plan. To say this plan is going to work.” Adebayo says his manifesto will improve the lives of Nigerians. According to him, fixing the government will fix the security challenges in the country. The SDP candidate said that Nigerians should not see terrorists anymore in six months, given the capacity of the Nigerian Armed Forces. Adewole promises to address banditry, saying that citizens will get security as a Christmas present in 2027. The presidential election is scheduled to be held on January 16, 2027. The post Tinubu, Atiku, Obi Will Collapse Under Their Own Weight — SDP’s Adewole appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 2027: ‘Tinubu Is Fit To Go,’ APC National Chairman Dismisses Claims Challenging President’s Health — Nentawe Yilwatda
item.description: The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Nentawe Yilwatda, has dismissed concerns about President Bola Tinubu’s health ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that the President is fit to contest. The APC chairman stated this on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday. ﻿ He urged Nigerians not to interpret isolated expressions of dissent against the President as evidence of widespread unpopularity. Addressing concerns about Tinubu’s limited attendance at some presidential campaign rallies, Yilwatda said the President could not be expected to participate in every campaign activity while discharging his constitutional responsibilities. He said some public officials had been advised to attend selected rallies rather than all the engagements to prevent governance from suffering. Following Tinubu’s earlier announcement that he would not attend every campaign rally because of the responsibilities of his office, the APC chairman said the President’s absence should not be interpreted as a sign of weakness or inability to lead the party’s re-election effort. Muslim-Muslim Ticket Yilwatda also defended the Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket of Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima, dismissing concerns that the arrangement would marginalise Christians under the APC administration. He maintained that Christians had continued to have their voices heard in government, adding that those the party had engaged were comfortable with the arrangement. “Most Christians that we’ve engaged and we’ve spoken to them, they are very okay with the Muslim-Muslim ticket,” he said. “The thought and the fear of most Christians was that the Muslim-Muslim ticket may suppress their voices, but their voices are heard loud and clear now.” He also argued that Christians had not suffered molestation because of Tinubu’s religion during the President’s three years in office. ADC Crisis Reacting to the Federal High Court judgment invalidating the David Mark-led leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), the APC chairman denied that his party had any involvement in the opposition party’s internal crisis. He questioned why the ADC was blaming the ruling party over a legal dispute instituted by one of its members. Asked whether he was pleased that the ADC was facing a leadership crisis, Yilwatda said he was not bothered by the development. Yilwatda expressed confidence that Tinubu would defeat Atiku in a free and fair election. He argued that Atiku’s performance in the 2023 presidential election was largely attributable to the political structure of the PDP rather than his individual popularity. “He did not win because of Atiku; he won because of the structure of the PDP. It was the PDP that brought Atiku, not Atiku winning on his own,” he said. item.title: What To Know About Nvidia CEO Spy Scandal
item.description: Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, whose chips power the global AI boom and who has the ear of President Donald Trump, has admitted to an affair with a Chinese executive who US intelligence reportedly believes was working for Beijing. Here is what we know: What Happened? Huang, 63, acknowledged the relationship Sunday in a message to Nvidia employees. “I was unfaithful to my wife,” he wrote. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Huang has been married to his wife Lori since 1985. His admission followed reports in The New York Times that US intelligence officials had concluded the woman, Alice Huang, was passing information to China. She is not related to the Nvidia chief. Nvidia had previously said that his interactions with her were “not unusual or unexpected” given their business ties. Who Is Alice Huang? Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a senior executive at Megaspeed. The Singapore-based data centre company was spun off from a Chinese company in 2023, and it rents out computing power from Nvidia chips. This screengrab from video footage by CTI obtained via the AFPTV on November 9, 2026 shows Alice Huang (2nd R in pink), a Chinese executive linked to the data centre company called Megaspeed, attending a dinner hosted by Nvidia’s chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang (2nd L in black back facing camera) at a restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025, during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. Photo by – / VARIOUS SOURCES / AFP The Wall Street Journal reported that she and Huang were photographed together in Taipei in 2024 and 2025. According to the Times, a memo circulated among senior US officials this spring cited intelligence that she was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. The memo said she had been recruited to gather information on Huang and possibly to steer Nvidia toward pushing for its top chips to be sold in China. The Journal said that authorities in Singapore and Taiwan also suspected Chinese intelligence had recruited her after learning of her closeness to Huang. Her current whereabouts are unclear. US officials suspect Megaspeed of helping smuggle restricted chips into China, and the Justice Department has taken over a federal investigation into the company. Megaspeed has previously described itself as a “compliant and legitimate company.” Beijing rejected the allegations. Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said Monday that “the narrative of a so-called Chinese spy is entirely baseless vilification and smearing.” Why Does It Matter? Nvidia controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for the chips used to train and run AI models. Washington has restricted sales of the most advanced ones to China since 2022 under the Biden administration. Huang has also been one of Trump’s most influential informal advisers on AI. item.title: Nvidia Shares Plunge As Board Probes CEO Over China Spy Reports
item.description: AI chip behemoth Nvidia was plunged into turmoil Monday after CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged having an affair, with reports saying US officials believe the woman was spying for China. Beijing denied the claim, but shares of the chipmaker tumbled after Nvidia’s board opened an inquiry into reports that Huang was “the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” Near 1610 GMT, Nvidia shares were down 5.5 percent after losing nearly nine percent earlier in the session. (FILES) The logo of Nvidia is seen during a production preview exhibition in Taipei on May 21, 2025. (Photo by I-HWA CHENG / AFP) Late last month, The New York Times reported that US intelligence officials determined that Alice Huang, a Chinese executive linked to Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, had been funneling information to Beijing. This screengrab from video footage by CTI obtained via AFPTV on November 9, 2026 shows Alice Huang (2nd R in pink), a Chinese executive linked to the data centre company called Megaspeed, attending a dinner hosted by Nvidia’s chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang (2nd L in black, back facing camera) at a restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025, during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. Photo by – / VARIOUS SOURCES / AFP The executive, also known as Huang Le and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Jensen Huang, developed a close relationship with him, the Times said. “I was unfaithful to my wife,” Huang said in a message to company employees. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Jensen Huang is a central figure in the AI boom and a close informal adviser to US President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly opposed regulating the industry so as not to let China gain the upper hand. The Times said Alice Huang’s relationship with the Nvidia chief could have given her insights into Trump’s thinking around AI. Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing Monday that “the narrative of a so-called Chinese spy is entirely baseless vilification and smearing.” AI is likely to come up when Trump meets President Xi Jinping later this month at a summit in China. ‘You Never Know’ Asked Sunday whether Huang would join the president’s Asia trip, which includes the Asia-Pacific summit in Shenzhen, Trump told reporters: “I don’t know, but I’ll certainly take him.” Trump said Huang was “a fine person, but you never know what’s going on. I’m sure — I hope everything’s fine. He’s done such an incredible job.” Nvidia’s board said in a statement Sunday it had opened an independent probe “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” “While the board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the board’s inquiry will examine all available information,” it said. item.title: Turkey Steel Factory Explosion Kills 16, Injures 13
item.description: An explosion ripped through a steel plant in western Turkey on Monday, killing 16 people and injuring 13, President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said, announcing investigations into the tragedy. Eight workers were trapped at the HABAS steel factory about 60 kilometres (37 miles) north of the port city of Izmir, where the blast struck around midday (0900 GMT), said Izmir governor Suleyman Elban. Footage posted online showed a huge cloud of thick smoke pouring into the sky as flames appeared to engulf a tall structure within the HABAS Demir Celik plant in Aliaga. “The circumstances surrounding this tragic incident, which has deeply saddened our nation, including how and why it happened, whether there was any negligence, and who bears responsibility, will be established,” Erdogan said on television. Turkey’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan talks with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung during their meeting at the presidential Blue House in Seoul on November 3, 2026. Photo by JEON HEON-KYUN / POOL / AFP He said two of the injured were in serious condition. HABAS is a privately owned group and one of Turkey’s top steel producers. Crane Collapse According to Izmir’s governor, the blast was caused by an overhead crane that collapsed into a large industrial furnace used during the liquid steel casting process. “While a boiler replacement operation was being carried out at the HABAS iron and steel factory, the overhead crane fell and landed in the arc furnace, causing an explosion in the steel mill behind it,” Elban told reporters, referring to a large electric-powered steelmaking furnace. An eyewitness, Deniz Ulker, said it felt like an “earthquake”. “When I looked at the factory across the street, thick black smoke was coming out. A fire broke out where the chimney was,” Ulker told Anadolu news agency. “It was like a bomb going off,” said Turan Ilbay, who works as a truck driver at the factory and also spoke to Anadolu. Izmir mayor Cemil Tugay said on X that rescue teams were “continuing their work to remove the collapsed platform” and that those affected were factory workers. Safety Issues Workers’ groups said there was a long record of safety issues at HABAS. Contacted by an AFP journalist, HABAS declined to answer questions. Before Monday’s explosion, the Evrensel daily said at least 11 workers had died over the past decade while working there. Turkey’s Labour Party, a small Marxist faction, said on X it was the third time in three weeks that workers had lost their lives at HABAS. It said one man died after falling eight metres (26 feet) from a ladder on October 21, while another died when a tyre he was inflating on a construction machine exploded.
